title: Binary COPY at run scale and index-backed queries
question: How fast do binary COPY writes of 100,000 observations and 20,000 claims go, and do the D3 queries stay index-backed at run scale (D3 §11)?
method: A finished full run of 2,500 synthetic units: 12,500 tasks, 100,000 observations in the D3 §6.2 shapes (16 mention, 8 relation, 8 scope, 7 value, 1 claim_proposal per unit; proposals are the v1 reference batches cycled), 5,000 entities, 20,000 claims with v1 qualifiers, supports and evidence; all by binary COPY with Copy.set_types; queries at that volume; run deletion at volume. No S2 or S3 outputs exist yet, so payloads are synthetic. PostgreSQL 18.6 (Ubuntu 18.6-1.pgdg24.04+2), pg_textsearch 1.5.1, vector 0.8.7, on the project-local cluster (just db-up; socket build/pg/run, port 5440, pg_textsearch preloaded); DDL applied and rows written as the NOLOGIN non-superuser cs_s6_app (SET ROLE) in cs_spike_s6 cloned from cs_template; psycopg 3.3.6 (binary), pgvector-python 0.5.1, spike venv checked against the lock (`uv sync --locked --check`: no changes) before the final run; free disk 109G at start, 106G at end.

agents.separation: coordinator brief; wrote only code/s6_*, code/s6*.py/.sql, results/s6/, records/s6.*

results.name: copy_observations_ms
results.note: 90116 rows/s; mean payload 297 B (mention mean 138 B; relation mean 205 B; scope mean 238 B; value mean 262 B; claim_proposal mean 4295 B)

results.name: float8_into_real_binary_copy
results.note: D6 §3's note confirmed: a real column needs float4

results.name: str_into_declared_jsonb
results.note: dumped as a JSON string, not parsed: pass dicts

results.name: why_a_method_ran_ms
results.note: seq scan of ops.task on unit_key (no index); fine at 10^4 tasks per run

results.name: run_deletion_ms
results.note: 5,000 entities and 20,000 claims with cascades; RI checks on claim subject/object/statement by skip scan; run and tasks kept

conclusion: Binary COPY writes 100,000 observations in about 1.1 s and 20,000 claims in about 0.2 s on the interim cluster; D6 §3's float4 requirement holds. At run scale the qualifier query is carried by claim_pred without a GIN index and stays near 1 ms; 'why a method ran' scans the run's tasks for lack of a unit_key index, under 1 ms at 12,500 tasks; deleting a run's 25,000 materialized rows takes about 0.27 s and keeps its run and tasks.
